source.title: STaR: Sensitive Trajectory Regulation for Unlearning in Large Reasoning Models
source.authors: Jingjing Zhou; Gaoxiang Cong; Li Su; Liang Li

record.tranche_reason: It evaluates unlearning efficacy and robustness using R-TOFU metrics and prompt paraphrasing, a conceptual test of the claim in large reasoning models rather than a direct reproduction of the cited studies.
record.gate_note: Table 3 directly tests paraphrased prompts. Table 1 reports answer-forgetting efficacy and retain-set utility, but does not report targeted-knowledge accuracy against a chance baseline. Its MCS results concern alternate decoding strategies, not the prompt-only attacks specified in the claim versions; these are recorded under fits_no_version. Table 2's membership-inference AUCs measure membership signals rather than recovery of targeted knowledge. Table 5 ablates STaR components, not an activation direction.
record.test_reason: Table 3 measures answer forgetting efficacy (AFE) for four parameter-updating unlearning methods and the new STaR method under paraphrased versus original prompts. That bears directly on prompt-only recovery (E), on the robustness half of A, and on a counter-method's resistance (F). The method differs from the originals: R-TOFU on a reasoning model, scored by similarity-based AFE.
record.authors_conclusion: Accurate. The authors conclude that STaR, a parameter-free inference-time filter, gives decoding-robust suppression of sensitive content in reasoning models. They report it beats GA/GD/KL/PO on forgetting, MCS and membership-inference metrics with high retain utility, and resists prompt paraphrasing.
record.recipe_differences: STaR is an inference-time, parameter-free trajectory and token suppression pipeline, unlike the parameter-updating unlearning methods it compares against.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports that baseline AFE drops under paraphrased prompts; STaR's AFE also declines from 0.88 to 0.82. MCS and forgetting metrics are also reported separately across forget01, forget05, and forget10.

fits_no_version.finding: STaR shows higher worst-case multi-decoding consistency (MCS) than GA/GD/KL/PO across forget01/05/10. The text says baselines leak forgotten content under ZeroThink/LessThink decoding.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Reasoning-model unlearning via parameter updates leaks forgotten content under alternative decoding modes (ZeroThink/LessThink); an inference-time filter reduces this.

record.problems: The experiments use one 8B backbone and a synthetic benchmark. No chance-level targeted-knowledge accuracy or unlearned-model comparison is reported, and the paraphrase metric is AFE rather than a direct measure of recovered knowledge. No uncertainty estimates are supplied.
record.rows_left_out: Table 2 MIA-A/MIA-C is omitted because membership-inference AUC measures sample-membership leakage, not recovery of targeted knowledge. Table 5 is omitted because it ablates STaR components rather than an internal activation direction or a knowledge-recovery attack. Table 1 CFE and other metrics are omitted because they measure CoT forgetting or aggregate performance rather than the answer-level target accuracy and paraphrase recovery captured in the included rows. Table 3 original-prompt values are recorded as baselines in rows r46-r50 rather than duplicated as separate rows.

untested.parts: Targeted-knowledge accuracy relative to chance; general capability beyond R-TOFU retain-set utility. No pre-unlearning AFE/MU reference is given.
Activation-direction ablation; any analysis of blocking versus deletion.
Jailbreaks, other languages and in-context information. Paraphrase tested only on forget01.
STaR's resistance to relearning, internal edits, quantization, jailbreaks, other languages, in-context attacks, and removal of the inference-time filter. STaR leaves the weights unchanged.

record.verdict_notes: Rows r01–r30 are correctly cannot_determine for A: AFE/MU are similarity-based with no chance or pre-unlearning reference. STaR modifies no weights; it detects forget-set queries and suppresses tokens at decode time. Its F support therefore concerns output suppression against paraphrase only; by design the knowledge remains in the weights. The study does not analyze this, so no C verdict is given. Single backbone (DeepSeekR1-Distill-Llama-8B), synthetic benchmark, no uncertainty estimates. Table 1 calls the fourth baseline PO, while the text calls it DPO.

versions.untested_parts: The study reports answer-forgetting efficacy and retain-set utility, but not targeted-knowledge accuracy relative to chance or whether recovery attacks succeed.
No post-unlearning fine-tuning or relearning set is tested.
No activation-direction ablation or analysis showing that an unlearning method blocks access rather than deleting knowledge is reported.
No low-bit quantization attack is tested.
Only paraphrased prompts are tested; jailbreaks, other languages, and in-context information are not tested.
STaR is evaluated against prompt paraphrasing. Resistance to relearning, internal edits, quantization, jailbreaks, other languages, and in-context information is not tested.

The AAAI 2026 copyright line suggests a venue that the record lists as not stated.

statements.correction: Attacks in 2601.09281: paraphrased prompts (Table 3, forget01 only). MCS = 1 - max leakage over DefaultThink, ZeroThink, LessThink, reported for GA, GD, KL, PO and STaR (Table 1). MIA-A/MIA-C membership inference (Table 2). No fine-tuning, quantization or internal-edit attacks.
statements.problem: Right that no fine-tuning, quantization or internal-edit attack is run. Wrong that this study probes reasoning-model knowledge only with paraphrases: MCS also measures worst-case leakage across decoding modes for all methods.

statements.correction: Query form: paraphrased prompts lower AFE (higher = more forgetting) for GA 0.57->0.31 and PO 0.68->0.37. R-TOFU forget01, DeepSeekR1-Distill-Llama-8B, Table 3.
